title: Bridge specification (call-site fact semantics) — v1.0
description: plan.md §8.2/§8.3, chainlink #22. One per crates/*/specs/_bridges/<bridge_id>.json. A caller postcondition holds only AFTER the caller returns -- it cannot establish a callee precondition at an earlier call site. The real obligation is: caller preconditions AND caller invariants AND path condition AND prior call results IMPLY callee precondition. available_contract_facts therefore has no 'caller-postcondition' role in its enum -- the schema makes the unsound shortcut structurally impossible to write, the same discipline plan.md §5.2's computed eligibility and chainlink #17's disjoint claim/evidence-method enums already use elsewhere in this pipeline. bridge_logic (§8.3) is the typed replacement for prose bridge_logic: prose cannot support machine assurance (the harness may assert a weaker property, fidelity can't be checked, and the result can't show the declared bridge was actually checked).

bridge_id.description: Must equal the filename stem exactly (G1b, enforced by scripts/validate_bridge.py), same discipline as boundary_id/interaction_id.

boundary_id.description: The boundary contract this bridge proves a call-site implication for. Cross-referenced to a real, promoted boundary contract in the same crate (G2, scripts/validate_bridge.py) -- not checked structurally by this schema.

callee_requirement.description: <Concept>.<id> -- the specific callee_guarantees entry (docs/boundary-contract-schema.json) this bridge discharges. Must be one of boundary_id's own callee_guarantees (G2, cross-referenced) and must equal bridge_logic.conclusion.obligation_id exactly (G1b, checked structurally here -- the human-readable summary and the machine-checkable conclusion can never silently diverge).

available_contract_facts.description: Facts genuinely available at the call site (plan.md §8.2): caller preconditions, invariants, previously-established callee postconditions, trusted environment assumptions. Deliberately has no 'caller-postcondition' role -- a caller postcondition only holds after the caller returns, so it can never be a fact available before the callee is invoked.

required_local_facts.description: Facts established locally at the call site (branch conditions, loop invariants, argument predicates) that aren't already a caller/callee contract obligation. Optional -- not every bridge needs one.

target_expression.description: The concrete call being discharged, e.g. "TaskQueue.C001(args, callee_state)". Free text at the schema level -- deeper expression structure is bridge_logic's job, not this field's.

protocol_class.description: Same vocabulary as docs/interaction-schema.json's own field -- a bridge for a non-pairwise edge discharges one step of a multi-step protocol, not the whole thing.

role.description: Deliberately excludes 'caller-postcondition' -- plan.md §8.2: 'the enclosing caller postcondition is normally not among them,' since it only holds after the caller returns.

bridge_logic.description: plan.md §8.3's typed expression form -- the machine-checkable replacement for prose bridge_logic. Generating a verifier harness from this representation is chainlink #22's own follow-up (harness codegen), tracked separately -- this schema only fixes the representation harness generation would compile from.

bindings.description: Name -> type. A binding's value is either a bare type name (e.g. caller_self: Scheduler) or a nested named group of typed sub-bindings (e.g. args: {now: Time}), matching plan.md §8.3's own worked example exactly.
